The pan‑Slavic song “Hey, Slavs” (“Hej Slaveni”) became the official national anthem of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on **2 December 1945** – the day the new constitution was promulgated and the anthem was adopted as a temporary, then permanent, national symbol. It remained in use (with a brief interim in 1946‑1947) until the breakup of Yugoslavia in the early 1990s.

**Answer: December 2 1945**  

The pan‑Slavic song “Hey, Slavs” (“Hej Slaveni”) became the official national anthem of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on **2 December 1945** – the day the new constitution was promulgated and the anthem was adopted as a temporary, then permanent, national symbol. It remained in use (with a brief interim in 1946‑1947) until the breakup of Yugoslavia in the early 1990s.
